name: Sweatshirt sleep hack

lead: The sweatshirt sleep hack means folding a sweatshirt over the eyes and top of the head and loosely looping the sleeves behind the head for sleep, as a makeshift eye mask and light blocker. It went viral on TikTok in January 2024.

The appearance chain is sleep to looks: darker, more comfortable sleep may mean better rest, which people associate with a fresher face and less puffiness. No studies have tested this specific practice.

paras: Practitioners fold the sweatshirt body over the eyes, leave the nose and mouth uncovered, and loop the sleeves loosely under the chin or behind the head, as a free alternative to a sleep mask.

Doctors quoted in news coverage mention overheating, skin irritation and restricted airflow if the wrap is tight or covers the nose and mouth, and some viewers reported feeling panicked or suffocated.

chain: Sweatshirt blocks light and gently wraps the head
angle.text: The hack is a no-cost way to make a sleep mask using existing clothing; the appearance benefit comes through better sleep, which practitioners say they experience but which has not been tested in studies.

lead: The sweatshirt sleep hack is an informal practice of draping a folded sweatshirt over the eyes and head and looping its sleeves around the head at bedtime, so that it works as a makeshift sleep mask.[1] Users connect darker, more comfortable sleep with a more rested look the next day, including fresher-looking skin and eyes.

The practice spread after TikTok creator Callie Galey posted a video of it on 20 January 2024; Bustle reported nearly 2.5 million likes and more than 10,000 comments by April.[1] Physicians quoted in coverage compared it to swaddling and a weighted blanket, while also noting overheating and airflow concerns.[1] No published studies have examined the practice itself.

paras: In the viral video, the sweatshirt is folded in half and held with the sleeves hanging down; the folded section goes over the eyes with the nose and mouth left clear, and the sleeves are looped loosely under the chin and tucked behind the head.[1] Galey called it comfortable and said it gave her the best sleep of her life, and when asked how she came up with it she answered "Desperation."[1]

Dr. Jessica Andrade, a physician quoted by Bustle, said the wrap works like swaddling, which can feel comforting, and that the pressure may create a cocoon effect similar to a weighted blanket; she added that extra fabric can cause overheating, particularly with a fluffy sweatshirt.[1]

Sleep expert Dr. Shelby Harris, also quoted by Bustle, described it as essentially a do-it-yourself sleep mask that likely blocks light less completely than a purpose-made one and does not stay in place as well; she noted that looping sleeves under the chin may restrict airflow and that fabric may irritate skin, and said trying it is reasonable if it stays loose, cool and does not affect breathing.[1]
Some commenters on the video said the wrap made them feel panicked or suffocated, and others noted that it would not suit side or stomach sleepers.[1]

timeline.event: Callie Galey posts the sweatshirt sleep video on TikTok on 20 January; news outlets cover the trend through the spring.[1]
